findings.detail: The plan's `chunk_0152:3` citation for the B_K definition is VALID under the current 206-chunk Simpson numbering -- verified BY CONTENT, not by number, per the renumbering hazard warning. chunk_0152.md contains the construction verbatim: W' = {(w,d) | w in W and d in D_w}; (w,d) <=' (w',d') iff w <= w' and d = d'; (w,d) R' (w',d') iff w = w' and R_w(d,d'). This matches the dispatch's transcription EXACTLY -- no OCR/plan conflict to flag. Lemma 8.1.2 is in the same chunk. The plan's other cited chunk (chunk_0068, Thm 3.3.4) was not needed by Phases 16-17 and was not checked.

The dispatch and plan cite cs5FC''/cs5FC/cs5FCIncest as all at CKExtension.lean:159,184. Only cs5FC (line 159) and cs5FC'' (line 184) are there. cs5Incest (CS5Canonical.lean:234) and cs5FCIncest (CS5Canonical.lean:255) live in CS5Canonical.lean instead. Minor and non-blocking -- the probe imports CS5Canonical, which pulls in CKExtension transitively. Worth correcting in future plan revisions.

The plan specifies proving the conjuncts 'given R_w refl/symm/trans and <=-monotonicity R_w subseteq R_w''. TWO refinements. (1) ADDITION: Dmono (D_w subseteq D_w', domain monotonicity) is required and is recorded as an ILModel field -- B_K's <=' moves the world component, so every freshly-constructed B_K-world needs a domain proof at the HIGHER context. This is not an addition to the source: Simpson's own box clause quantifies over d' in D_w' at w' >= w, presupposing exactly this. (2) OMISSION: a conjectured Rdom (R w d e -> D w e) turned out to be UNNECESSARY and was deliberately left out -- every conjunct that produces a fresh world reuses the SOURCE world's label, so Dmono alone transports domain membership. The hypothesis set is therefore minimal, which strengthens the result.

CONFIRMS the plan's guardrail claim, as required by the dispatch. BKR makes R' a label-level, WITHIN-context relation over an arbitrary K: R' relates labels d,d' inside one fixed context w (w = w' is definitional in BKR), never two theories. By contrast cs5Incest_forces_symm (CS5Canonical.lean:643) and cs5TwoSidedR_iff_cs5Tail (CS5Canonical.lean:511) are both statements about the CANONICAL model's theory-to-theory relation. This probe never mentions, constructs, or quantifies over theories, so neither guardrail is instantiable here and neither fires. The independence is load-bearing: B_K |= cs5FC'' is established over EVERY IL-model, so it cannot be an artifact of any canonical-model-specific collapse. This is mechanized in the file's module docstring, not merely asserted in prose.

BK_not_cs5FC is stronger and simpler than the plan anticipated. cs5FC's <=-composed transitivity (r w u -> u <= u' -> r u' t -> r w t) is instantiated at w := (w,d), u := (w,d), u' := (w',d), t := (w',d): BOTH r-premises are mere REFLEXIVITY instances of R', so the obstruction needs no cleverly-placed edge -- it needs only R_w's reflexivity plus two distinct <=-comparable contexts. The conclusion would be (w,d) R' (w',d), whose first component is w = w', contradicting w != w'. Structural reason: <=' moves the world and pins the label; R' moves the label and pins the world; the two never compose into the cross-context edge cs5FC demands.

Every load-bearing result (BK_cs5FC'', BK_cs5Incest, BK_cs5FCIncest, BK_not_cs5FC) is abstract over an arbitrary K and uses no such construct.
